title: Getting Better at Working With You: Compiling User Corrections into Runtime Enforcement for Coding Agents
title_zh: 与你协作得更好：将用户纠正编译为编码 Agent 的运行时强制约束
abstract_en: Interactive LLM agents are becoming part of daily work, but they do not reliably become easier to work with over time: a correction remembered in one session may still be violated in the next. We study this gap between preference access and preference compliance. In tasks derived from anonymized real-user friction cases, Mem0 memory still leaves 57.5% of applicable preference checks violated. We introduce Test-time Rule Acquisition and Compiled Enforcement (TRACE), a drop-in skill-layer pipeline for coding-agent runtimes that mines user corrections, rewrites them as atomic rules, and compiles them into runtime checks that must pass before an agent completes future tasks. Unlike runtime checks written ahead of time by developers, TRACE skills come from the user's own chat corrections. We evaluate TRACE with simulated user-in-the-loop experiments on ClawArena coding-agent tasks and MemoryArena-derived memory-intensive tasks. On ClawArena, TRACE reduces held-out preference violation from 100.0% to 37.6% on in-distribution tasks and from 100.0% to 2.0% on out-of-distribution tasks. On MemoryArena-derived tasks, TRACE reduces in-distribution violation from 100.0% to 60.5% while matching or exceeding the strongest memory baseline on task pass. These results suggest that compiling corrections into runtime enforcement can address a repeated-friction failure mode that memory alone does not reliably solve, reducing the need for users to restate the same correction across future sessions. Experiment code is available at https://github.com/YujunZhou/TRACE_exp, and the deployable skill is available at https://github.com/YujunZhou/tellonce.
abstract_zh: 交互式 LLM agents 正逐渐融入日常工作，但它们并不会稳定地“越用越懂用户”：某次会话中已被纠正的偏好，下一次仍可能被违反。本文研究“能访问偏好”与“能遵守偏好”之间的差距。在源自匿名真实用户摩擦案例的任务中，即使使用 Mem0 memory，仍有 57.5% 的适用偏好检查被违反。作者提出 Test-time Rule Acquisition and Compiled Enforcement（TRACE），一种可即插即用的 coding-agent runtime skill-layer pipeline：它从用户纠正中挖掘规则，将其改写为原子化规则，并编译成运行时检查，要求 agent 在完成未来任务前必须通过。不同于开发者预先编写的 runtime checks，TRACE 的规则来自用户自己的聊天纠正。作者在 ClawArena coding-agent 任务和 MemoryArena 衍生的记忆密集型任务上进行模拟用户在环实验。结果显示，在 ClawArena 上，TRACE 将 held-out 偏好违反率在同分布任务中从 100.0% 降至 37.6%，在分布外任务中从 100.0% 降至 2.0%；在 MemoryArena 衍生任务中，TRACE 将同分布违反率从 100.0% 降至 60.5%，同时在任务通过率上达到或超过最强 memory baseline。结果表明，将纠正编译为运行时强制约束，可以缓解仅靠记忆难以解决的重复摩擦问题，减少用户在未来会话中反复重申同一纠正的需要。
key_points_zh: 问题聚焦于 coding agents 的“偏好访问 vs 偏好遵守”差距：即使 agent 记住了用户偏好，也可能在后续任务中继续违反。
TRACE 从用户聊天纠正中自动挖掘偏好，改写为原子规则，并编译为运行时检查，在 agent 提交结果前强制执行。
与传统 memory 方法不同，TRACE 不只是存储偏好，而是将其转化为可验证的 enforcement mechanism，从而降低重复违规。
在 ClawArena 上，TRACE 将 held-out 偏好违反率从 100.0% 降至同分布 37.6%、分布外 2.0%，显示出较强泛化能力。
在 MemoryArena 衍生任务上，TRACE 仍能降低偏好违反率，并在任务通过率上匹配或超过最强 memory baseline。

llm_assessment.comment: TRACE is highly relevant because it converts user corrections into persistent runtime enforcement, directly addressing reusable agent compliance and evolution.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: TRACE 将用户纠正编译为持久运行时约束，直接解决了智能体合规性和持续改进问题。
